Our client has a confidential pending liability (Tenbrook regulatory probe) that we must not disclose. The terms regarding duration of confidentiality (3 years) and term (24 months) seem reasonable but we could request a minor clarification for better protection. Since this is the initial draft, we should accept most terms but suggest a slight tightening on description of confidential information and remedies to benefit our client. We must avoid disclosure of the client’s hidden liability and keep the draft professional and non-confrontational to advance negotiations.

Please see our edits for your consideration. We look forward to your feedback to move this forward.

drafter.private_reasoning: Opposing counsel wants to narrow the definition of Confidential Information to exclude information already public or independently developed, and consistent alignment of confidentiality obligations and term. To keep our client's undisclosed regulatory probe protected as confidential, we accept narrowing but carefully word exclusions, and align confidentiality duration to three years survival as currently proposed. We remove the prior conflicting term clause of 24 months. We explicitly exclude information already publicly known or independently developed to meet their point without compromising our client's information. We reiterate injunctive relief availability to strengthen remedies. We do not disclose the Tenbrook probe.

We believe these modifications offer balanced protection for both parties while addressing your concerns.
